settings.weight: Design files + 0.5 per existing test + 1 per new test; the turn budget counts Design files only

edges.reason: U-6 states that "a `publishedTitle` conflict is re-thrown for U-26 to map to a 422 title error (AC-16)".
U-7 states that it "lets a `publishedTitle` conflict surface as P2002 for U-26".
U-19 states that a title "already used by another published article: 422 `{ errors: { title: [...] } }` through U-26 (AC-16)".
U-20's published-update branch promises 422 `{ errors: { title: [...] } }` for a changed title that is already published (U-20, SC-9); only U-26 produces that body from U-7's P2002.

test_intents.intent: a published row renders `draft: false` and a draft row `draft: true`, with every other field and its order unchanged.

`draft: true` with a title and empty or absent description/body is accepted; missing or empty title gives the 400 body error; a non-boolean `draft` and non-string fields are 400; a published create still requires title, description and body.
optional title/description/body/tagList plus an optional boolean `draft` pass, while syntax errors answer 400 body errors; the draft-state title rule is left to the endpoint (U-20).

the private address is title-independent and stable; the title-derived address appends `-2`, `-3`, ... until unused in both the slug space and the retained private-address space; a collision is retried.

the editor shows `Save as draft` and `Publish Article`; a draft save needs only a title (empty description/body allowed) and does not submit the published form; both actions and the fields are disabled while a request is pending, so a second save/publish cannot start.
a draft preview shows a visible `Draft` badge and no favorite control; a published preview renders exactly as today.

the signed-in author's own profile shows a separate Drafts tab that requests that author's drafts at 10 per page with the page offset and marks entries; another profile renders no Drafts tab and makes no drafts request; a drafts 404 leaves the drafts view; changing tabs resets to page 1.

an author's draft shows `Draft`/`Not published`, Edit/Delete/Publish, no favorite/follow/comment controls and no comment request; publish sends only `draft: false`, is disabled while pending, and a 422 title error leaves the marked draft with its content; a published article shows no draft marker and no unpublish control; a 404 from publish redirects home without content.
Save as draft calls create with `draft: true` and opens the returned private address; a 400/422 body error is shown and the editor content is kept; empty description/body do not block the draft save.

a draft offers both actions: save stays on the private address with content changed, publish navigates to the returned title-derived address; a published article offers only the published update and no draft action; 422 title/published errors keep the draft view and are shown.

create/update send the editor's `draft` flag, the drafts request carries author/limit/offset and decodes `draft`, publish sends only `{ article: { draft: false } }`, and 422 field-keyed `title` or `published` errors plus 400 `{ errors: { body: [...] } }` decode as field errors.

an authenticated title-only `draft: true` create answers 201 with `{ article }` carrying `draft: true` and empty description/body; a missing or empty title answers 400 with field errors and stores nothing; an unauthenticated save answers 401 and stores nothing; a published create still needs description and body.

the author reopens the private address and sees the stored draft; a `draft: true` update with changed title/description/body/tags answers 200 with `draft: true` and the same private address, while a title-less draft save answers 400 with no stored change.

publishing a title-only draft answers 200 with `draft: false`, a title-derived address carrying `-2` when that address is taken, the publishing moment as `createdAt`, and the stored description/body; the article is then first in newest-first lists.

publishing a draft whose title is already published answers 422 with `{ errors: { title: [...] } }` carrying a title-taken message, creates no publication, and leaves the draft and the existing article unchanged.

a `draft: true` update of a published article answers 422 with `{ errors: { published: [...] } }` and changes nothing; `draft: false` and omitted updates keep it published and apply the published update without creating a draft.

a published create using a draft's title succeeds with a title-derived address that takes a suffix when needed; two drafts with the same title coexist with distinct private addresses; saving a draft with a published title succeeds.

publishing the same draft twice, the second time through its old private address, answers 200 with the already published article, one row, the first slug and `createdAt`, and no duplicate address or entry.

a draft save overlapping the publish marker or locked transaction answers 422 with `{ errors: { published: [...] } }`; whichever ordering occurs, the final row is published with its first publishing date and one address, with no duplicate publication.

a Visitor and an Other User read a draft's private address as 404 with no article data and the draft unchanged; the Author reads 200 with `draft: true`; the old private address after publication is 404.

the author's drafts list (author omitted or equal to the caller) returns only that author's drafts, all `draft: true`, most recently updated first, 10 per page with the author's total drafts count; the public author list returns published only; another author's drafts request or a request with no signed-in caller answers 404; invalid paging/author answers 400 `{ errors: { query: [...] } }`.
the global, author, tag and favorites lists and their counts, plus the followed-authors feed and its count, exclude drafts for every caller and page; pagination uses the published-only total.
a tag used only by a draft is absent from `GET /api/tags` and appears once a published article uses it.
every Other User update or delete addressed to a draft answers 404 with the draft unchanged; an unauthenticated write answers 401; no related record is created.

favoriting, unfavoriting and commenting on a draft answer 404 for every signed-in user including the Author and 401 anonymously, with no favorite, comment or count change; comment reads return an empty list to the Author and 404 to others.

the author's draft delete answers 200 with the deleted body and `draft: true`, later reads answer 404, and the row never appears in a published list, count or tag; deleting through a published row's retained private address answers 404 and leaves the article.

after the seed is run a second time exactly one seed-marked alice draft with the decided title/description/body/tag exists, other alice drafts are untouched, it is absent from published lists/counts and from popular tags, and it is present in alice's drafts query; the temporary round-trip create passes `draft: false` explicitly.

the three seeded articles stay published with their existing `createdAt`/`updatedAt` and list order, no pre-feature row becomes a draft, and the seed leaves comments, users, tags and relations intact.

the global feed still shows exactly the three seeded published articles and the `typescript` tag, with no seeded draft title and no `draft-notes` tag; alice's profile drafts list shows the seeded draft while a visitor's and bob's article lists do not.

signed in as the author, `/editor` with a title only saves a draft and lands on the private page marked `Draft`/`Not published`; the profile's drafts tab lists it; reopening it, changing the body and saving keeps the marker and the new content; publishing shows the article as published, it leaves the drafts list and appears in the published/global list.

an empty title shows the title error and starts no draft save, while a blank description and body still save a title-only draft; deleting the draft from its page sends the author home, removes it from the drafts list and leaves no public entry.

an author's draft page offers no favorite/follow/comment control; a Visitor and an Other User opening the draft address are sent home with no draft content; the Other User's profile shows no Drafts tab and opening its `/drafts` address goes home.

a draft whose title is already published stays a marked draft with its content after a publish attempt that shows the title-taken error; a published article's page shows no unpublish or save-as-draft control; a draft and a published article with the same title each appear in their proper place with the draft marked.
with the draft open in two tabs, a save overlapping a publish from the other tab resolves to the published article shown without a draft marker and with no draft left in the drafts list.

on the author's own profile the Drafts tab is separate, lists only drafts most recently edited or saved first at 10 per page with the drafts count and marks every entry; the published and favorites tabs and another user's profile never list a draft, and another user's `/drafts` address goes home.

the home global, feed, tag, author-published and favorites lists show no drafts and their pagination follows the published-only counts; the popular-tags sidebar omits a draft-only tag and shows it after a published article uses it.

search.rule: base promotion (T1) before stubs (T2); fewest splits first; a bigger split replaces the choice only if T drops by >= 15%; a stub option needs the Planner's confirmation

planner.option_reason: Options 1 and 2 lower T only from 37.5 to 37.0 (1.3%), far below the required 15%, while each adds two stubbed units and an extra split. The no-stub base U-1, U-3, U-4, U-26 is kept.
planner.notes:
- The four kept reliance edges are exactly the 422 title-field mapping. U-8 is dropped because it detects an existing published title itself and returns `title-taken`, which U-20 maps; only the P2002 paths of U-6, U-7 and the endpoints U-19/U-20 need U-26. U-26 is already in Option 0's base, so callers do not have to wait.
- The api and ui specs must use fresh users, titles and tags, clean up after themselves, and never edit or delete alice's seeded draft (AC-20); the AC-20 intent re-runs the seed before its assertions so idempotency is exercised.
- The ui intents are the only tests that exercise the cut http edges for U-32, U-33 and U-35; every unit intent mocks the other side, so it proves presentation only.
- `packages/db/src/article/articleSlug.test.ts` is the only new unit file and it sits next to a U-5 Design file; the other unit intents extend the listed existing files and add the `draft`/`published` fixtures the Design Notes call for.
- AC-18 is proven across the api intents (it requires the server to be the enforcement point); no separate product code is added for it.
